evidence: (a) No equivalent rule found: CURRENT-DESIGN.md:23-26 establishes live structural reconciliation and member provenance; :47-49 and DESIGN-NOTES.md:283-289 define undo by the original action's created objects/added relationships, preview, and conflict handoff, but do not classify later template-derived members. (b) The conflict handoff is an accepted fallback, not an explicit decision that every later derived member is a conflict; DESIGN-NOTES.md:274,289 expressly leave dependency checks open. (c) Hydration undo and live templates are both in scope (CURRENT-DESIGN.md:23,47-48). (d) Material: hydrate H into an existing team, then a template edit adds B through H's live reference (DESIGN-NOTES.md:209,219). B was not created by H, while undo must reverse H's contribution and preserve unrelated work (CURRENT-DESIGN.md:47-48). The design does not establish whether B survives, retires, or blocks undo, so it cannot yet classify or preview this ordinary history consistently. This confirms the narrow acknowledged dependency/cascade design gap, not that the draft promises unconditional safe inversion or that the recorded creation set is the sole available evidence; CURRENT-DESIGN.md:49,55 already flags exact dependency checks and cascade restoration as open.
